decidedBy: an agent reading each verse of Luke on the project owner's instruction to name whom the text names, 2026-10-29
policy: Where Luke's narrator, or someone speaking to him, calls Jesus the Lord, ὁ κύριος names Jesus. The κύριος of a parable and the Lord of the Old Testament quotations are not ruled.
source: Essenthos, Luke's 'the Lord' read against each verse by claude-opus-5-5 on the project owner's instruction, 2026-10-29

rulings.why: 'And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her' (LUK 7:13): Jesus, who raises the widow's son at Nain (7:11-15).
'Mary, which also sat at Jesus' feet' (LUK 10:39): the Lord at whose feet she sits is Jesus, whom Martha received (10:38).
'And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha' (LUK 10:41): the Lord who answers Martha is Jesus.
'And the Lord said unto him, Now do ye Pharisees' (LUK 11:39): Jesus, at the Pharisee's table (11:37).
'And the Lord said, Who then is that faithful and wise steward' (LUK 12:42): Jesus answering Peter (12:41); the second κύριος of the verse is the steward's lord in the parable and is not ruled.
'The Lord then answered him, and said, Thou hypocrite' (LUK 13:15): Jesus, who healed the woman on the sabbath (13:10-14).
'And the apostles said unto the Lord, Increase our faith' (LUK 17:5): Jesus, whom his disciples address (17:1).
'And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed' (LUK 17:6): Jesus answering the apostles.
'And the Lord said, Hear what the unjust judge saith' (LUK 18:6): Jesus, telling the parable (18:1).
'And Zacchaeus stood, and said unto the Lord' (LUK 19:8): Jesus, at whose house Zacchaeus stands (19:5-7).
'Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor' (LUK 19:8): Zacchaeus addresses Jesus.
'And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter' (LUK 22:61): Jesus, as Peter denies him the third time.
'And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him' (LUK 22:61): Jesus' word of 22:34.
'The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon' (LUK 24:34): the risen Jesus.
